the dynamic population grating formed in ytterbiam-doped fiber enables the high-resolution adaptive optical sensor/demodulation of the phase modulation with a high-pass frequency response.

a dynamic grating with a high-pass frequency response can be formed in YDF by recording at a wavelength 1064 nm, and that this grating is associated with the changes in the UV absorption of the Yb3+ ions.

the proposed sensor/demodulation scheme can ensure a resolution of about 10-9 rad Hz-1/2 at the recording power of 10mW and can be scaled to a higher level with the increase of the recording power.
the dynamic population grating is an effective tool for adaptive interferometry with high resolution and sensitivity, especially for the phase modulation detection in the low frequency range.

the dynamic population grating in YDF enables the adaptive optical fiber interferometric sensor/demodulation with high sensitivity, dynamic range, and frequency resolution, and with a simple and compact configuration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the adaptive interferometric configuration with dynamic population gratings recorded at 1060–1080 nm in YDFs can be considered as a perspective tool for high-resolution interferometric sensors and demodulators.
the adaptive fiber sensor with a Sagnacs configuration can be realized by the YDF with a high-pass filter transfer function and with an excellent sensitivity.
we have shown the possibility to use the dynamic phase gratings for high-resolution optical sensing of phase modulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamic population grating can be effectively utilized for the adaptive interferometry with a high resolution and high modulation depth.
the YDF-based adaptive interferometric configuration can be used for the detection of phase modulations with high sensitivity, high spatial resolution, and high dynamic range.
the adaptive interferometer can be realized at 1064 nm using a dynamic phase grating recorded in a standard YDF.
